sourceType: Official Government of Punjab tourism website
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries are written in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Punjab's smallest district by area and population, in the cotton belt ('Land of White Gold'). Formed from Bathinda district in 1992. Three tehsils: Mansa, Budhlada, Sardulgarh.

places.name: Smadh of Bhai Gurdas
places.facts: Memorial to Bhai Gurdas, who founded Mansa town after renouncing worldly life here; annual March-April fair draws both Hindus and Sikhs.

places.name: Sardulgarh Fort
places.facts: Built by the Maharaja of Patiala; town renamed for Sardul Singh who hunted here; fort now houses the local police station.

places.name: Gurdwara Patshahi Nauvin
places.facts: Commemorates Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's visit.

places.name: Gurdwara Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib
places.facts: Associated with Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.

places.name: Gaushala and Picnic Spot, Khokar Kalan
places.location: Village Khokar Kalan, 7-8km from Mansa city
places.facts: Cow shelter with a park, lake, boating, children's area and temple.

places.name: Sardulgarh Thermal Plant
places.facts: Listed as an eco-tourism/industrial interest site.

howToReach.rail: Mansa Railway Station, on the Bathinda-Jind-Delhi line
